plan.estimand: Main effect of 3-level factor in balanced 3-by-2 fixed factorial ANOVA (all 6 cells independent, full interaction model, common variance)
plan.hypothesis: H0: All levels of 3-level factor have equal population means vs. H1: At least one differs
assumptions: Balanced design: equal n per cell
Common variance across all cells (homogeneity of variance)
F-test for Factor A main effect with 2 numerator df
Partial eta-squared of 0.06 reflects effect size for Factor A main effect
missing_information: Conversion formula from partial eta-squared to non-centrality parameter λ for the F distribution (requires model-specific parameterization for factorial ANOVA with interaction)
clarification_questions: Should the partial η² = 0.06 be interpreted as the effect size in a model that includes the main effect of Factor B and the Factor A × B interaction?
Is the denominator df in the F-test expected to be (6 - 1)×(n - 1) = 5(n - 1), reflecting residual variation in all 6 cells?
scientific_notes: Partial eta-squared in factorial ANOVA is the proportion of residual variance explained by the factor, conditional on all other effects (main and interaction) being in the model.
Conversion to non-centrality λ: λ = [n × (# cells for tested factor) × η²_partial] / (1 - η²_partial) × (df_denom / df_numer), or equivalent parameterization from effect size literature.
The test statistic F = (MS_factor) / (MS_residual) ~ F(df_numer, df_denom, λ) under H1.
For a balanced 3×2 design with n per cell: total N = 6n, df_numerator = 2, df_denominator = 6(n-1).
